Affinity Ponzi Scam

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Investing for your nest egg can be scary, so who do you trust with your money? A respected Johannesburg accountant takes members of his community for tens of millions of rands and then disappears.

Unique Selling Point:
A classic ‘affinity fraud’ - a crime which targets a specific community, generally a religious community, often taking the form of a Ponzi scheme. In this case the majority of the members who were scammed were Jewish, but other people who were referred by family and word of mouth were also scammed. We see how easily people gave over their hard earned money and inheritance to a respected accountant Michael David Ash, whose son is a prominent charismatic Rabbi. How the victims were ostracised by the community for speaking out. This is South Africa’s Bernie Madoff story.

Summary:
Johannesburg accountant Michael David Ash allegedly scammed community members out of at least R60 million, and then fled to Israel. A case of fraud was opened at the Sandringham Police Station in 2019.

There have been around 55 victims who were taken by this respected accountant, a trusted member of the Jewish community. He presented himself as a pious man whose son is a leading charismatic Rabbi in Johannesburg. But why does Rabbi Eitan Ash claim no knowledge of the fraud, when he tried to broker a settlement with one of the victims Andi Colley? The rabbi signed a sworn affidavit at the Sandringham Police station stating that he had no knowledge after supposedly trying to broker a settlement. According to the investigator who has 8 victims under this case, these were just stalling tactics until Michael Ash fled the country. Once he disappeared, the Rabbi closed ranks and told them to do what they had to do – that is, lay charges.

Before fleeing the country Chad Thomas confronted Michael Ash, recorded on video, where he admits that the money was not invested in Steinhof which is what he told one of the victims, quickly changed his story to it was invested in the President’s game farm, and then said no it wasn’t invested and he would pay the money back. This of course did not happen. We will try and confront the Rabbi to get some answers. A call to Michael Ash in Israel and speak to some of the victims who have lost their savings.


Further information:
One of the victims, 66 year old Andi Colley, is also the aunt of the Rabbi through marriage. She has been left destitute. She invested 2 million rand with Michael Ash and was paid interest of R16000 a month for about two years, and then the interest payments abruptly stopped. This money was all Andi had to live on. Now penniless, she is unable to pay her bills and is struggling to survive. She suffers from extreme depression as a result of this.

In around 2019, she engaged the services of Forensic Investigator Chad Thomas of IRS to try and retrieve her money.

“I was asked to accept an offer to be given half back, and to sign a non-disclosure agreement that would implicate me in the crime. I chose not to do this, and contacted Chad Thomas of IRS Forensic Investigations last September. We have been working on [the case] since then. I was told to wait to receive a payout, but eventually realised it would never be made. That’s when I laid criminal charges.”

Andi Colley also wrote a letter about the matter to Chief Rabbi of South Africa Dr Warren Goldstein.

Thomas went to Michael Ash’s home to ask for proof as to where the money was invested, this he recorded on video. Michael Ash first said it was Steinhoff and then when he was asked for proof of this, he changed the story to the investment being in the President’s farm Phala Phala. After a bit of back and forth he openly admitted that the money was never invested. One wonders if this narrative by Michael Ash was spurred on because there is a video on Facebook of his son the Rabbi with the President, where the president endorses Eitan Ash as an upstanding member of society and someone he would want to keep close to him.

Shortly after this confrontation, Mr Ash’s son Rabbi Eitan Ash, approached Andi Colley and tried to settle with her by saying that his dad would pay back R1 Million rand of the 2 Million rand she had invested with him as she had received some funds already. The irony is the funds she had received were supposed to be interest on the capital amount, not part of the capital amount. They soon realised it was a stalling tactic, and Michael Ash fled the country shortly after.

Another set of victims who are not Jewish, but were referred by a cousin who had invested with Michael Ash are Philip and Wendy Wadsworth. Wendy’s father had invested around R4M rand with Michael Ash and for a short while received payment of around R55 000 per month. This enabled Richard Fletcher and his wife to live comfortably on their savings for a short while. During this time Philip Wadsworth engaged the services of Michael Ash as his accountant, and saw that it would be a good investment to also put in around 4.5 million rand of his savings with Michael. They were supposed to be in a 5 year investment plan, When Philip wanted to buy a house five years later cash, he asked for R1 Million of his money, to which Michael said he had re-invested it for another 5 years and that Philip should try and get a bond for his house. They started to smell a rat when the payments to Wendy’s father stopped and there were a myriad of excuses as to the money being stuck with SARS etc.. then they started hearing that other people they knew eg Andi Colley hadn’t received their money back and after many attempts to recover their money from Michael Ash failed, they joined Andi and a few others to lay charges on Michael after he had fled the country. In the meantime Wendy’s mother had passed away and her parents were living hand to mouth and struggling as their life investment had been lost.

Another set of victims Laura Trapedo, who is widowed and her three children were also taken by Michael. Laura is the sister of Andi Colley and also the aunt of Rabbi Eitan Ash. They now live in Israel but are prepared to do a video call with us. Laura invested R500 000 and never had it returned or received any interest on the money. Her three children received an inheritance of R1M from their grandmother and they got back R500 000, and then the money repayments stopped. They are a struggling family who too have been left destitute. Andi’s other sister Tessa and her husband were also taken but they are refusing to speak out about it, as they are embarrassed and don’t want to bring the Jewish community and the Rabbi into disrepute. They and the community ostracised Andi when she originally spoke out. There is a Jewish law, Loshon-Hora, that states you can’t speak ill of your community, but it really means gossip or harm, but many Jewish people believe that this is about protecting the broader Jewish community.

But where does this leave the desperate victims and why is no one willing to follow up on the case? Apparently the police are in the process of doing a 205 on Michael Ash’s bank accounts which was apparently actioned in 2020, but there has been no feedback to date. This is according to Andi Colley. Chad Thomas says the wheels of justice are turning slowly with the COVID backlog and other priority cases. But the case has been referred to the NPA and it is with the Hawks. The Prosecutor appointed to the case is Sandra Mart.

Another man whose brother was a victim and had cancer at the time, was promised by Ash that he would get his money back. About 350 emails and more than two years later, the brother has died, and his family has been left with nothing. This man has suffered two heart attacks from stress. (he wants to remain anonymous)

We would confront the Rabbi Eitan Ash, (Ash’s son) and ask where his father is and how can they leave these community members destitute? He needs to answer as to why when they made an original offer to settle with Andy Colley, it fell away after his father fled to Israel and there has been no attempt to pay back any of the funds that were misappropriated by the victims. We would speak to the police, get a response from the Hawks and the NPA as to the status of the case.

The question is, why is there no motivation to bring an obvious Ponzi scheme con artist to book? Why is his son the Rabbi an upstanding member of the community committed perjury in his affidavit to the police claiming no knowledge of his father’s wrongdoings? If he refuses to respond, I think we should try the Chief Rabbi of Johannesburg, as Andi Colley has written to him and has received no response. I am trying to get a number for Michael Ash in Israel, as I think it would be great if we could call him, he may answer the phone and we can push him for answers. It think it is important in this story that the Chief Rabbi does respond, as both of Michael Ash’s sons, Eitan and Menachem are rabbis, and the family does hide under a cloak of religiosity.

South Africa has an extradition treaty with Israel which was tested successfully in July 2016 when Rabbi Eliezer Berland was formally extradited from South Africa to Israel,” according to IRS. But getting it done in reverse is a lot harder.

Press Release:


A smokescreen of lies.// A respected Joburg accountant takes his community for tens of millions of rands - leaving their nest eggs ransacked.

Script:


VO: There is something to say about - Tradition // A kinship built on trust and values/ The Johannesburg Jewish Community lives by these age-old principles. // This is the story of a devout member of that community who betrayed that trust // Accountant Michael David Ash

Chad: What happened to her money, sir?
Ash: It went into a farm with the President.

Andi: He struck me as a very, very religious Jewish Hasidic man. His children had been educated at the Hasidic school, in Johannesburg,I thought that he was a financial adviser.

Wendy: You know, he had quotes, you know, respect thy Father and, you know, things like that. I mean, his one son's a Rabbi,
Philip: He was a registered chartered accountant And on the sideline, he does these kinds of investments.
LINK: Think Bernie Madoff, America's biggest Ponzi scheme. Whilst not on that scale, this has similar hallmarks - somebody using his connections in his community, promising big returns on investments all the while robbing Peter to pay Paul

VO: As long as there's enough cash to go around, the scam lives on.

Chad: During 2018, we were approached and advised that there was an alleged Ponzi scheme, targeting primarily members of the Jewish community.

VO: Financial Crimes Investigator Chad Thomas confronts fraud daily.

Chad: It ticked a lot of the boxes of what one would expect in a Ponzi scheme, we were then engaged to investigate the matter.

The Hook
REPUTATION AND TRUST

LINK: In a close-knit community reputation is everything. And so when Andi Colley a divorcee returned from overseas with a little bit of money, she needed guidance on how to invest it. One name kept coming up. Michael Ash.

Andi: I had invested my life savings, my retirement benefits, which had been cashed in. And an inheritance, with Mr. Ash.His brother married my sister. And this was in the late 1970s.// My sister said that he'd been investing money for a large portion of the community in which we live and that it yielded good returns, and that he was very honest.
Bongani Bingwa: Did he tell you what he was investing in?
Andi: No, he said he did bulk investments for many people at a time.

Chad: We call it an affinity scam. And affinity is an extension of a Ponzi. And that means that the majority of the victims come from a specific community.

The Sell
REASONABLE RETURNS, MEDIUM RISK

VO: Sold on a medium-risk investment, Andi took the plunge with her first one-and-a-half million rand.

Andi: Every month, I got 16,000 rand at first.

VO: For four years the interest on her capital flowed in. Come 2018, she topped it up with another half a million.

Andi: After I had invested the 500,000 it was increased to 19,200 per month, which is about right.

VO: But the paperwork was sketchy - no business letterhead and her investment appeared to be a loan on which she was earning interest.

LINK: Gaining people's trust, that was easy for Michael Ash to do, after all, his reputation preceded him. But he was much more than that. He was the kind of guy who could work his way into people's homes and their hearts. And that's exactly what he did to the Wadsworths. Hello, guys. Good to meet you. Thank you.

VO: At first, Ash would become Philip Wadsworth’s company accountant, a recommendation through family connections.

Philip: From an accounting point of view my company ran beautifully and perfectly.
VO: When he presented them with an investment opportunity they didn't hesitate; After all, Wendy’s parents were receiving R50 000 a month from their deal with Ash

Wendy: He spoke about a whole load of things regarding investing the money
Bongani Bingwa: he gave you companies?
Wendy: I remember one of them was Coca-Cola. I remember that vividly. He knew the talk.
VO: So in 2010, their 1 million rand safely tucked away for 5 years, promised to grow to just over one and a half million - they planned to buy a house with it.

Philip: 23rd of September 2014. We gave him a further 3.4 million.

VO: 2015 - The moment of truth, time for their first payout - the one and a half million or so -

Philip: He reinvested that, without consulting with us. And then he said to me, he will help me to get a home loan, a new home loan.
Bongani Bingwa: And that seemed okay to you?
Philip: We didn't really… I didn't really know what to say at the time, because he'd sort of spun so many stories around and got your head in such a muddle that all our money was tied up.

THE SMOKESCREEN
Ducking & Diving

Wendy: But then we started to realize he’s avoiding us like the plague Once he had shingles, the once his car broke down,// BEAT// he was avoiding my parents too

VO: The Michael Ash well was running dry.//

VO: With around 7 million invested, now the fifty thousand rand monthly returns her parents, June and Richard Fletcher were getting - simply stopped.


Richard: This is my … my pension. And now that 6.7 million suddenly turned to nothing, absolutely nothing.

VO: A master at the game - Ash reassured his clients with what he told them was a bank-guaranteed cheque for their invested amounts. // But was it worth the paper it was written on? //


Richard: when the payment didn't come in, I surrendered that cheque
Bongani Bingwa: to the bank…
Richard: to the bank. They said sorry. In fact, it was declined. Return to sender.
Chad: Ultimately, what happens in any Ponzi scheme is they run out of investors. And I think that's what was happening between 2016 and 2018. A lot of people were asking for money, and there just wasn't enough in the kitty to pay them.

// BEAT //
VO: Red flags were everywhere! Andi tried to cash in a separate 100,000 rand investment - Michael Ash didn't honour the deal.//
Panicked, she appealed to his son, the prominent Rabbi Eitan Ash, seen here in 2022 with President Cyril Ramaphosa.

SOUND UP: Eitan Ash Facebook video]
Ramaphosa: I draw a lot of inspiration from people like Rabbi Ash.

Andi: Eitan Ash became involved - He put the 100,000 Rand into my bank account saying I must be very appreciative that he paid it out of his own pocket because most people got nothing back.

VO: At least she still had her 2 million rand to look forward to, maturing in 2019. But in August 2018 - her monthly payments stopped. So she called Michael Ash.

Andi: He told me that his cell phone had been left on the plane to Israel and that he could not release the payment because he could not get the OTP.

VO: The yarns kept on spinning - the money was lost in a deal in President Ramaphosa's Game Farm and of course the Steinhoff scandal, South Africa's biggest corporate fraud.

THE BLACK SWAN EVENT

Chad: So fraudsters always look to what we call black swan events, to be able to say, Listen, something's gone wrong. We can't pay back your money. With Steinhoff, it became a convenient scapegoat.

Bongani Bingwa: You've lost everything?
Andi: I have.He’s left me poverty-stricken.

VO: Andi fought back - acting on her behalf, Chad Thomas paid Ash a visit…with evidence that he wasn't a registered financial advisor.

CHAD THOMAS - MICHAEL ASH CONFRONT
Chad: Sir did you make the trade to Steinhoff? Let's be honest with one another
Michael: Did I make.. no.. the the.. what?
Chad: Did you invest her money in Steinhoff, sir?
Michael: No, no
Chad : What happened to her money sir?
Michael: It went into a farm with the President, I had a share in his game farm
Chad: So let's not beat around the bush here
Michael: I'm not, I'm telling you the truth
Chad: So you did not invest her money in Steinhoff?
Michael: No, I didn't
Chad: You told her you did though.
Michael: I told her, uh, no I told her I said that the platform went wrong, okay so I did.
Chad: So you did, so you misrepresented the facts to her. What are we going to do sir?
Michael: Well, I'm going to pay her back.

Chad: I left. I had given him my business card. And that night, I got a call from his son, Eitan Ash
VO: They all agreed to meet.

Chad: And then the story just became more bizarre. He said to me, it was a high-risk, high-return Lending Scheme.
Bongani Bingwa: Did he concede that this was illegal?
Chad: Just in the fact that he's now talking about having a lending book and he's not registered with the National Credit regulator, is an admission of doing something untoward. But what what was strange again, is he couldn't provide me with the debtors book.

VO: Michael Ash paid Andi 30 000 rand, then sent her a settlement offer - but only for half of her 2 million rand capital amount. // But here's the rub, she had paid tax to the tune of three hundred thousand rand on what she thought were earnings.

Andi: I didn't want to accept this paltry offer (nice pause and emotion from her here) I wanted to take it further.
Bongani: And did you?
Andi: I did indeed.
//beat//

Chad: During our investigation, we found out that there could be upwards of 40 victims and in total, we represented about eight parties. // But by the end of our investigation, we're looking at close to about 100 million Rand that we believe had been misappropriated through misrepresentations.

VO: Joining the fightback, the Wadsworths - but it had come at a heavy price, the stress took its toll on Wendy.

Bongani Bingwa: What was the hardest part for you?
Philip: We'd been to hell and back with her health… it’s been
Bongani Bingwa: I'm sorry
Philip: But we managed to get through it she's nowhere near as bad as what she used to be - cries

VO: And the ultimate heartache, the loss of a beloved mom and wife. June Fletcher, passed away, with their nest egg plundered.

TITLE: THE ESCAPE

VO: The word was out - In early 2019 Michael Ash left for Israel. And Andi's settlement offer seemed off the table -

Chad: By June, we realized Michael was not coming back.

VO: So the only avenue left, was to lay criminal charges against Michael Ash //
Rabbi Eitan Ash refused to answer our questions but responded that he has always conducted himself appropriately in matters concerning his father and that they are estranged.
Beat//Montage Israel
We've been unable to make contact with Michael Ash in Israel. // But his victims live in hope, that the authorities will catch up with him.
beat//

Andi: He's a liar. A cheat. A thief, in fact, I would call him evil.

Philip: He should be stripped bare naked put in an orange suit and locked up alive. put in Max prison, bread and water simple as that.
VO: That time may come, but for now, the one thing Michael Ash does have over Bernie Madoff - he's managed to escape.

The Prosecutor appointed to the case is Sandra Mart. Another man whose brother was a victim and had cancer at the time, was promised by Ash that he would get his money back. About 350 emails and more than two years later, the brother has died, and his family has been left with nothing. This man has suffered two heart attacks from stress. (he wants to remain anonymous) We would confront the Rabbi Eitan Ash, (Ash’s son) and ask where his father is and how can they leave these community members destitute? He needs to answer as to why when they made an original offer to settle with Andy Colley, it fell away after his father fled to Israel and there has been no attempt to pay back any of the funds that were misappropriated by the victims. We would speak to the police, get a response from the Hawks and the NPA as to the status of the case. The question is, why is there no motivation to bring an obvious Ponzi scheme con artist to book? Why is his son the Rabbi an upstanding member of the community committed perjury in his affidavit to the police claiming no knowledge of his father’s wrongdoings? If he refuses to respond, I think we should try the Chief Rabbi of Johannesburg, as Andi Colley has written to him and has received no response. I am trying to get a number for Michael Ash in Israel, as I think it would be great if we could call him, he may answer the phone and we can push him for answers. It think it is important in this story that the Chief Rabbi does respond, as both of Michael Ash’s sons, Eitan and Menachem are rabbis, and the family does hide under a cloak of religiosity. South Africa has an extradition treaty with Israel which was tested successfully in July 2016 when Rabbi Eliezer Berland was formally extradited from South Africa to Israel,” according to IRS. But getting it done in reverse is a lot harder. 2023 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 19 May 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: A smokescreen of lies.// A respected Joburg accountant takes his community for tens of millions of rands - leaving their nest eggs ransacked. Script: VO: There is something to say about - Tradition // A kinship built on trust and values/ The Johannesburg Jewish Community lives by these age-old principles. // This is the story of a devout member of that community who betrayed that trust // Accountant Michael David Ash Chad: What happened to her money, sir? Ash: It went into a farm with the President. Andi: He struck me as a very, very religious Jewish Hasidic man. His children had been educated at the Hasidic school, in Johannesburg,I thought that he was a financial adviser. Wendy: You know, he had quotes, you know, respect thy Father and, you know, things like that. I mean, his one son's a Rabbi, Philip: He was a registered chartered accountant And on the sideline, he does these kinds of investments. LINK: Think Bernie Madoff, America's biggest Ponzi scheme. Whilst not on that scale, this has similar hallmarks - somebody using his connections in his community, promising big returns on investments all the while robbing Peter to pay Paul VO: As long as there's enough cash to go around, the scam lives on. Chad: During 2018, we were approached and advised that there was an alleged Ponzi scheme, targeting primarily members of the Jewish community. VO: Financial Crimes Investigator Chad Thomas confronts fraud daily. Chad: It ticked a lot of the boxes of what one would expect in a Ponzi scheme, we were then engaged to investigate the matter. The Hook REPUTATION AND TRUST LINK: In a close-knit community reputation is everything. And so when Andi Colley a divorcee returned from overseas with a little bit of money, she needed guidance on how to invest it. One name kept coming up. Michael Ash. Andi: I had invested my life savings, my retirement benefits, which had been cashed in. And an inheritance, with Mr. Ash.His brother married my sister. And this was in the late 1970s.// My sister said that he'd been investing money for a large portion of the community in which we live and that it yielded good returns, and that he was very honest. Bongani Bingwa: Did he tell you what he was investing in? Andi: No, he said he did bulk investments for many people at a time. Chad: We call it an affinity scam. And affinity is an extension of a Ponzi. And that means that the majority of the victims come from a specific community. The Sell REASONABLE RETURNS, MEDIUM RISK VO: Sold on a medium-risk investment, Andi took the plunge with her first one-and-a-half million rand. Andi: Every month, I got 16,000 rand at first. VO: For four years the interest on her capital flowed in. Come 2018, she topped it up with another half a million. Andi: After I had invested the 500,000 it was increased to 19,200 per month, which is about right. VO: But the paperwork was sketchy - no business letterhead and her investment appeared to be a loan on which she was earning interest. LINK: Gaining people's trust, that was easy for Michael Ash to do, after all, his reputation preceded him. But he was much more than that. He was the kind of guy who could work his way into people's homes and their hearts. And that's exactly what he did to the Wadsworths. Hello, guys. Good to meet you. Thank you. VO: At first, Ash would become Philip Wadsworth’s company accountant, a recommendation through family connections. Philip: From an accounting point of view my company ran beautifully and perfectly. VO: When he presented them with an investment opportunity they didn't hesitate; After all, Wendy’s parents were receiving R50 000 a month from their deal with Ash Wendy: He spoke about a whole load of things regarding investing the money Bongani Bingwa: he gave you companies? Wendy: I remember one of them was Coca-Cola. I remember that vividly. He knew the talk. VO: So in 2010, their 1 million rand safely tucked away for 5 years, promised to grow to just over one and a half million - they planned to buy a house with it. Philip: 23rd of September 2014. We gave him a further 3.4 million. VO: 2015 - The moment of truth, time for their first payout - the one and a half million or so - Philip: He reinvested that, without consulting with us. And then he said to me, he will help me to get a home loan, a new home loan. Bongani Bingwa: And that seemed okay to you? Philip: We didn't really… I didn't really know what to say at the time, because he'd sort of spun so many stories around and got your head in such a muddle that all our money was tied up. THE SMOKESCREEN Ducking & Diving Wendy: But then we started to realize he’s avoiding us like the plague Once he had shingles, the once his car broke down,// BEAT// he was avoiding my parents too VO: The Michael Ash well was running dry.// VO: With around 7 million invested, now the fifty thousand rand monthly returns her parents, June and Richard Fletcher were getting - simply stopped. Richard: This is my … my pension. And now that 6.7 million suddenly turned to nothing, absolutely nothing. VO: A master at the game - Ash reassured his clients with what he told them was a bank-guaranteed cheque for their invested amounts. // But was it worth the paper it was written on? // Richard: when the payment didn't come in, I surrendered that cheque Bongani Bingwa: to the bank… Richard: to the bank. They said sorry. In fact, it was declined. Return to sender. Chad: Ultimately, what happens in any Ponzi scheme is they run out of investors. And I think that's what was happening between 2016 and 2018. A lot of people were asking for money, and there just wasn't enough in the kitty to pay them. // BEAT // VO: Red flags were everywhere! Andi tried to cash in a separate 100,000 rand investment - Michael Ash didn't honour the deal.// Panicked, she appealed to his son, the prominent Rabbi Eitan Ash, seen here in 2022 with President Cyril Ramaphosa. SOUND UP: Eitan Ash Facebook video] Ramaphosa: I draw a lot of inspiration from people like Rabbi Ash. Andi: Eitan Ash became involved - He put the 100,000 Rand into my bank account saying I must be very appreciative that he paid it out of his own pocket because most people got nothing back. VO: At least she still had her 2 million rand to look forward to, maturing in 2019. But in August 2018 - her monthly payments stopped. So she called Michael Ash. Andi: He told me that his cell phone had been left on the plane to Israel and that he could not release the payment because he could not get the OTP. VO: The yarns kept on spinning - the money was lost in a deal in President Ramaphosa's Game Farm and of course the Steinhoff scandal, South Africa's biggest corporate fraud. THE BLACK SWAN EVENT Chad: So fraudsters always look to what we call black swan events, to be able to say, Listen, something's gone wrong. We can't pay back your money. With Steinhoff, it became a convenient scapegoat. Bongani Bingwa: You've lost everything? Andi: I have.He’s left me poverty-stricken. VO: Andi fought back - acting on her behalf, Chad Thomas paid Ash a visit…with evidence that he wasn't a registered financial advisor. CHAD THOMAS - MICHAEL ASH CONFRONT Chad: Sir did you make the trade to Steinhoff? Let's be honest with one another Michael: Did I make.. no.. the the.. what? Chad: Did you invest her money in Steinhoff, sir? Michael: No, no Chad : What happened to her money sir? Michael: It went into a farm with the President, I had a share in his game farm Chad: So let's not beat around the bush here Michael: I'm not, I'm telling you the truth Chad: So you did not invest her money in Steinhoff? Michael: No, I didn't Chad: You told her you did though. Michael: I told her, uh, no I told her I said that the platform went wrong, okay so I did. Chad: So you did, so you misrepresented the facts to her. What are we going to do sir? Michael: Well, I'm going to pay her back. Chad: I left. I had given him my business card. And that night, I got a call from his son, Eitan Ash VO: They all agreed to meet. Chad: And then the story just became more bizarre. He said to me, it was a high-risk, high-return Lending Scheme. Bongani Bingwa: Did he concede that this was illegal? Chad: Just in the fact that he's now talking about having a lending book and he's not registered with the National Credit regulator, is an admission of doing something untoward. But what what was strange again, is he couldn't provide me with the debtors book. VO: Michael Ash paid Andi 30 000 rand, then sent her a settlement offer - but only for half of her 2 million rand capital amount. // But here's the rub, she had paid tax to the tune of three hundred thousand rand on what she thought were earnings. Andi: I didn't want to accept this paltry offer (nice pause and emotion from her here) I wanted to take it further. Bongani: And did you? Andi: I did indeed. //beat// Chad: During our investigation, we found out that there could be upwards of 40 victims and in total, we represented about eight parties. // But by the end of our investigation, we're looking at close to about 100 million Rand that we believe had been misappropriated through misrepresentations. VO: Joining the fightback, the Wadsworths - but it had come at a heavy price, the stress took its toll on Wendy. Bongani Bingwa: What was the hardest part for you? Philip: We'd been to hell and back with her health… it’s been Bongani Bingwa: I'm sorry Philip: But we managed to get through it she's nowhere near as bad as what she used to be - cries VO: And the ultimate heartache, the loss of a beloved mom and wife. June Fletcher, passed away, with their nest egg plundered. TITLE: THE ESCAPE VO: The word was out - In early 2019 Michael Ash left for Israel. And Andi's settlement offer seemed off the table - Chad: By June, we realized Michael was not coming back. VO: So the only avenue left, was to lay criminal charges against Michael Ash // Rabbi Eitan Ash refused to answer our questions but responded that he has always conducted himself appropriately in matters concerning his father and that they are estranged. Beat//Montage Israel We've been unable to make contact with Michael Ash in Israel. // But his victims live in hope, that the authorities will catch up with him. beat// Andi: He's a liar. A cheat. A thief, in fact, I would call him evil. Philip: He should be stripped bare naked put in an orange suit and locked up alive. put in Max prison, bread and water simple as that. VO: That time may come, but for now, the one thing Michael Ash does have over Bernie Madoff - he's managed to escape.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Investing for your nest egg can be scary, so who do you trust with your money? A respected Johannesburg accountant takes members of his community for tens of millions of rands and then disappears.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A classic ‘affinity fraud’ - a crime which targets a specific community, generally a religious community, often taking the form of a Ponzi scheme. In this case the majority of the members who were scammed were Jewish, but other people who were referred by family and word of mouth were also scammed. We see how easily people gave over their hard earned money and inheritance to a respected accountant Michael David Ash, whose son is a prominent charismatic Rabbi. How the victims were ostracised by the community for speaking out. This is South Africa’s Bernie Madoff story.
metadata.Summary: Johannesburg accountant Michael David Ash allegedly scammed community members out of at least R60 million, and then fled to Israel. A case of fraud was opened at the Sandringham Police Station in 2019. There have been around 55 victims who were taken by this respected accountant, a trusted member of the Jewish community. He presented himself as a pious man whose son is a leading charismatic Rabbi in Johannesburg. But why does Rabbi Eitan Ash claim no knowledge of the fraud, when he tried to broker a settlement with one of the victims Andi Colley? The rabbi signed a sworn affidavit at the Sandringham Police station stating that he had no knowledge after supposedly trying to broker a settlement. According to the investigator who has 8 victims under this case, these were just stalling tactics until Michael Ash fled the country. Once he disappeared, the Rabbi closed ranks and told them to do what they had to do – that is, lay charges. Before fleeing the country Chad Thomas confronted Michael Ash, recorded on video, where he admits that the money was not invested in Steinhof which is what he told one of the victims, quickly changed his story to it was invested in the President’s game farm, and then said no it wasn’t invested and he would pay the money back. This of course did not happen. We will try and confront the Rabbi to get some answers. A call to Michael Ash in Israel and speak to some of the victims who have lost their savings.
metadata.Further information: One of the victims, 66 year old Andi Colley, is also the aunt of the Rabbi through marriage. She has been left destitute. She invested 2 million rand with Michael Ash and was paid interest of R16000 a month for about two years, and then the interest payments abruptly stopped. This money was all Andi had to live on. Now penniless, she is unable to pay her bills and is struggling to survive. She suffers from extreme depression as a result of this. In around 2019, she engaged the services of Forensic Investigator Chad Thomas of IRS to try and retrieve her money. “I was asked to accept an offer to be given half back, and to sign a non-disclosure agreement that would implicate me in the crime. I chose not to do this, and contacted Chad Thomas of IRS Forensic Investigations last September. We have been working on [the case] since then. I was told to wait to receive a payout, but eventually realised it would never be made. That’s when I laid criminal charges.” Andi Colley also wrote a letter about the matter to Chief Rabbi of South Africa Dr Warren Goldstein. Thomas went to Michael Ash’s home to ask for proof as to where the money was invested, this he recorded on video. Michael Ash first said it was Steinhoff and then when he was asked for proof of this, he changed the story to the investment being in the President’s farm Phala Phala. After a bit of back and forth he openly admitted that the money was never invested. One wonders if this narrative by Michael Ash was spurred on because there is a video on Facebook of his son the Rabbi with the President, where the president endorses Eitan Ash as an upstanding member of society and someone he would want to keep close to him. Shortly after this confrontation, Mr Ash’s son Rabbi Eitan Ash, approached Andi Colley and tried to settle with her by saying that his dad would pay back R1 Million rand of the 2 Million rand she had invested with him as she had received some funds already. The irony is the funds she had received were supposed to be interest on the capital amount, not part of the capital amount. They soon realised it was a stalling tactic, and Michael Ash fled the country shortly after. Another set of victims who are not Jewish, but were referred by a cousin who had invested with Michael Ash are Philip and Wendy Wadsworth. Wendy’s father had invested around R4M rand with Michael Ash and for a short while received payment of around R55 000 per month. This enabled Richard Fletcher and his wife to live comfortably on their savings for a short while. During this time Philip Wadsworth engaged the services of Michael Ash as his accountant, and saw that it would be a good investment to also put in around 4.5 million rand of his savings with Michael. They were supposed to be in a 5 year investment plan, When Philip wanted to buy a house five years later cash, he asked for R1 Million of his money, to which Michael said he had re-invested it for another 5 years and that Philip should try and get a bond for his house. They started to smell a rat when the payments to Wendy’s father stopped and there were a myriad of excuses as to the money being stuck with SARS etc.. then they started hearing that other people they knew eg Andi Colley hadn’t received their money back and after many attempts to recover their money from Michael Ash failed, they joined Andi and a few others to lay charges on Michael after he had fled the country. In the meantime Wendy’s mother had passed away and her parents were living hand to mouth and struggling as their life investment had been lost. Another set of victims Laura Trapedo, who is widowed and her three children were also taken by Michael. Laura is the sister of Andi Colley and also the aunt of Rabbi Eitan Ash. They now live in Israel but are prepared to do a video call with us. Laura invested R500 000 and never had it returned or received any interest on the money. Her three children received an inheritance of R1M from their grandmother and they got back R500 000, and then the money repayments stopped. They are a struggling family who too have been left destitute. Andi’s other sister Tessa and her husband were also taken but they are refusing to speak out about it, as they are embarrassed and don’t want to bring the Jewish community and the Rabbi into disrepute. They and the community ostracised Andi when she originally spoke out. There is a Jewish law, Loshon-Hora, that states you can’t speak ill of your community, but it really means gossip or harm, but many Jewish people believe that this is about protecting the broader Jewish community. But where does this leave the desperate victims and why is no one willing to follow up on the case? Apparently the police are in the process of doing a 205 on Michael Ash’s bank accounts which was apparently actioned in 2020, but there has been no feedback to date. This is according to Andi Colley. Chad Thomas says the wheels of justice are turning slowly with the COVID backlog and other priority cases. But the case has been referred to the NPA and it is with the Hawks. The Prosecutor appointed to the case is Sandra Mart. Another man whose brother was a victim and had cancer at the time, was promised by Ash that he would get his money back. About 350 emails and more than two years later, the brother has died, and his family has been left with nothing. This man has suffered two heart attacks from stress. (he wants to remain anonymous) We would confront the Rabbi Eitan Ash, (Ash’s son) and ask where his father is and how can they leave these community members destitute? He needs to answer as to why when they made an original offer to settle with Andy Colley, it fell away after his father fled to Israel and there has been no attempt to pay back any of the funds that were misappropriated by the victims. We would speak to the police, get a response from the Hawks and the NPA as to the status of the case. The question is, why is there no motivation to bring an obvious Ponzi scheme con artist to book? Why is his son the Rabbi an upstanding member of the community committed perjury in his affidavit to the police claiming no knowledge of his father’s wrongdoings? If he refuses to respond, I think we should try the Chief Rabbi of Johannesburg, as Andi Colley has written to him and has received no response. I am trying to get a number for Michael Ash in Israel, as I think it would be great if we could call him, he may answer the phone and we can push him for answers. It think it is important in this story that the Chief Rabbi does respond, as both of Michael Ash’s sons, Eitan and Menachem are rabbis, and the family does hide under a cloak of religiosity. South Africa has an extradition treaty with Israel which was tested successfully in July 2016 when Rabbi Eliezer Berland was formally extradited from South Africa to Israel,” according to IRS. But getting it done in reverse is a lot harder.
